t.1.186.1: Food for the bridegroom's party has been prepared by King Drupada for the sake of the wedding. Having completed all your tasks, come there and partake of it, you and Kṛṣṇā too; there must be no delay.
t.1.186.2: These chariots, bright with golden lotuses, yoked with fine horses and worthy of lords of the earth, are for you. Mount them, all of you, and go to that residence of the king of the Pāñcālas.
t.1.186.3: Then those bulls among the Kurus set out, having first sent that priest ahead and mounting those great chariots; and Kuntī and Kṛṣṇā went along together with them.
t.1.186.4: Having heard from the purohita the words which the Dharmarāja had spoken, O Bhārata, he then, wishing to find out who these best of the Kurus truly were, gathered together many kinds of objects.
t.1.186.6: Whatever things there might be pertaining to the other crafts, all of them were arranged there in their entirety; and whatever things served for play and amusement, all those too the king brought there.
t.1.186.5: Fruits and finely made garlands, hides, coats of mail and seats, cows too, O king, and ropes, and other articles for the purpose of farming.
t.1.186.7: There were gleaming armours for chariots and horses, great swords, and splendid horse-drawn chariots, excellent bows and choice arrows, and spears and lances adorned with gold.
t.1.186.8: There were lances, bhuśuṇḍis and battle-axes, and likewise everything needed for warfare; and there too were beds and seats of many kinds, finely crafted.
t.1.186.9: Kuntī, taking the virtuous Kṛṣṇā with her, entered Drupada's inner apartments, and the women, high-spirited, received with honor her, the wife of the Kaurava king.
t.1.186.11: The king and all the king's ministers, the king's sons and likewise his friends, and all his servants, every one of them, O king, were filled with exceeding joy there.
t.1.186.12: Then those heroes, foremost among men, sat down there in due order upon the excellent, costly seats furnished with footstools, without hesitation and without showing any astonishment.
t.1.186.10: Having beheld those foremost of heroic men, whose gait was like the stride of lions, whose eyes were like those of great bulls, who wore deerskins as upper garments, whose lofty shoulders were thickly muscled, and whose long arms were like the coiled bodies of serpent-kings…
t.1.186.15: Perceiving that, Drupada's son and the king, together with all their chief ministers, approached in delight and honored the sons of Kuntī, the sons and grandsons of a king.
t.1.186.13: Various kinds of food fit for kings were served in vessels of gold and silver, as finely dressed male and female servants, along with the cooks, brought in the meal.
t.1.186.14: Having eaten there as much as they wished, those foremost heroes among men, greatly delighted, passed over all the riches there, and the heroes among men went straight to the implements of war.
